# bob albums

Inspect album notes

```text title="bob albums --help"
Inspect album notes

Bare `bob albums` runs the read-only list. `list` shows albums grouped by root. `check` lints albums against the contract. `sync` repairs generated records indexes and album catalogs in one guarded transaction. `tidy` moves album H1 titles into frontmatter `title`, as a dry run unless `-a` is passed. `create` makes an album with its Base and catalog rows in one guarded commit. `update` edits one album schema from a JSON envelope in one scoped commit.

Usage: bob albums [COMMAND]

Commands:
  check   Check albums against the contract
  create  Create an album with its Base and catalog rows
  list    List albums grouped by root (default)
  sync    Repair generated records indexes, record walks, and album catalogs
  tidy    Move album H1 titles into frontmatter `title` (dry run by default)
  update  Update an album record schema through a guarded JSON envelope

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Bare `bob albums` runs the read-only list.

Examples:
  bob albums                       List albums grouped by root
  bob albums list -r body          List one root's albums
  bob albums check                 Lint albums against the contract
  bob albums check -f json         Findings as JSON
  bob albums sync -d               Preview index repairs as diffs
  bob albums sync                  Repair every healthy album index
  bob albums tidy                  Preview title moves as diffs
  bob albums tidy -a               Move titles into frontmatter in one commit
  bob albums create body eat -n restaurant -s 'Places to eat.'
                                   Create eat.md with its Base and catalog rows
  bob albums update eat -i envelope.json
                                   Apply a guarded schema envelope

See docs/records.md for the album contract.
Run 'bob albums <command> --help' for more information on a command.
```

## bob albums check

Check albums against the contract

```text title="bob albums check --help"
Findings grouped by album and by owner catalog, plus an album/record/error/warning summary. Catalog warnings and damaged-region errors appear after album findings. Exits 1 on any error, 0 otherwise. This command is read-only.

Usage: bob albums check [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <DIR>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob albums check
  bob albums check -f json

See docs/records.md for the album contract.
```

## bob albums create

Create an album with its Base and catalog rows

```text title="bob albums create --help"
Create STEM.md at the vault root as an album owned by PARENT (an area or project of any status), with its starter STEM.base and every affected owner catalog row, in one guarded write and one scoped `albums: create <stem>.md` commit. STEM is lower-cased to a vault-root capture route. `-n` is required and follows the record noun rule; `-s` is required and a summary over 140 characters only warns. The title defaults to the humanized stem and the label to the noun-derived label. Validation or refusal exits 2.

Usage: bob albums create [OPTIONS] --noun <NOUN> --summary <SUMMARY> <PARENT> <STEM>

Arguments:
  <PARENT>
          Parent area or project (stem or path)

  <STEM>
          Album stem; names <stem>.md, <stem>.base, and <stem>/

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <DIR>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -d, --dry-run
          Print planned unified diffs; write nothing

  -e, --emoji <EMOJI>
          One-line emoji for the album and its rows

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

  -l, --label <LABEL>
          One-line record label; defaults to the noun-derived label

  -n, --noun <NOUN>
          Record noun matching [a-z][a-z0-9_]*

  -o, --open
          Open the new album in Obsidian after creating it

  -s, --summary <SUMMARY>
          One-line summary of what the album collects

  -t, --title <TITLE>
          One-line title; defaults to the humanized stem

Examples:
  bob albums create body eat -n restaurant -s 'Places to eat around here.'
  bob albums create fun movies -n movie -s 'Films.' -t Movies -e '🎬'
  bob albums create body eat -n restaurant -s 'Places.' -d
  bob albums create body eat -n restaurant -s 'Places.' -o

See docs/records.md for the album creation contract.
```

## bob albums list

List albums grouped by root (default)

```text title="bob albums list --help"
Albums grouped by root, with titles, record counts, group counts, freshness, and issue markers. The report also includes health for each generated `## Albums` owner catalog, including stale catalogs whose last album was removed. Run `bob albums sync` to repair catalog findings. This command is read-only. Bare `bob albums` runs this command.

Usage: bob albums list [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <DIR>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

  -r, --root <ROOT>
          Filter to one computed root identity

Examples:
  bob albums
  bob albums list
  bob albums list -r body -f json

See docs/records.md for the album contract.
```

## bob albums sync

Repair generated records indexes, record walks, and album catalogs

```text title="bob albums sync --help"
Repair each album's generated [!records] index, each record's walk line, and each owner's generated `## Albums` catalog from one snapshot. A real run takes the shared vault lock, pre-syncs, guards album declarations, record frontmatter, folder membership, and the owner/ancestor/declaration inputs catalog rows use, then makes one scoped commit `albums: sync (N notes)` when indexes, walk lines, or catalogs change. Current indexes, walk lines, and catalogs write and commit nothing and skip post-sync. `--dry-run` plans diffs without a lock or sync cycle. Damaged albums, damaged walk lines, and damaged catalogs are left intact, healthy regions continue, and any damaged region or runtime failure exits 1.

Usage: bob albums sync [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <DIR>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -d, --dry-run
          Print planned unified diffs; write nothing

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob albums sync
  bob albums sync -d
  bob albums sync -b ~/bob-work -f json

See docs/records.md for the index, catalog, and sync contract.
```

## bob albums tidy

Move album H1 titles into frontmatter `title` (dry run by default)

```text title="bob albums tidy --help"
Give each root album a bob-owned frontmatter `title` and drop its redundant H1. An album without `title` gains `title: <its current title>`, inserted after `type`: the first H1 before a bullet or `##` (wikilinks to display text), else the first alias, else the humanized stem. Walk lines, `[!records]` indexes, and `[!albums]` catalogs therefore keep the same text. The first body H1 is then removed when it is the first body content outside fenced code and its text equals that title exactly. A differing H1, an H1 after other content, a later H1, and an H1 inside fenced code are kept and reported. An unusable `title` or damaged frontmatter leaves the album unchanged with a warning. Without `-a` the run is a dry run: it prints unified diffs and takes no lock, writes nothing, runs no Git, and does no sync. `-a` takes the shared vault lock, pre-syncs, replans, guards each album by its full preimage, verifies that each rewritten album keeps its title and plans no further change, makes one scoped `albums: tidy (N notes)` commit, and post-syncs only when it committed. STEM selects one root album by its exact stem. Caution: an older bob reads album titles only from the H1, so its `bob albums sync` would rewrite walk lines and catalog rows to the humanized stem; apply only after every host that runs album sync has this bob.

Usage: bob albums tidy [OPTIONS] [STEM]

Arguments:
  [STEM]
          Album stem; selects the root <stem>.md note

Options:
  -a, --apply
          Write the plan and make one verified commit

  -b, --bob-dir <DIR>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob albums tidy
  bob albums tidy eat
  bob albums tidy -f json
  bob albums tidy -a

See docs/records.md for the album title rule.
```

## bob albums update

Update an album record schema through a guarded JSON envelope

```text title="bob albums update --help"
Apply an ordered JSON schema envelope to one root album: validate ordered schema edits, preserve unrelated bytes, rebuild the generated index, replan affected record walk lines in the same transaction, and return safe inverse operations for Undo. The `walk_by.set` operation selects a declared single-value choices field for the walk order or uses null to unset it; the index keeps its independent ordering. A stem selects one root album, never a record noun fallback or an arbitrary path. `-i -` reads stdin, and omitted `-i` has the same meaning. A schema no-op previews without a lock or sync; a changed apply takes the shared vault lock, pre-syncs, replans fresh, and makes one scoped `albums: update <stem>.md` commit. Validation or semantic refusal exits 2; runtime, lock, or transaction failures exit 1.

Usage: bob albums update [OPTIONS] <STEM>

Arguments:
  <STEM>
          Album stem; names the root <stem>.md note

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <DIR>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -d, --dry-run
          Print planned unified diffs; write nothing

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

  -i, --input <FILE>
          JSON envelope file; - reads stdin (default)

Examples:
  bob albums update eat -i envelope.json
  cat envelope.json | bob albums update eat
  bob albums update eat -d -i envelope.json
  bob albums update eat -f json -i envelope.json

See docs/records.md for the update request and result contract.
```
